claim: For SuppressSourceGeneration = true types, members whose key comes from an attribute derived from KeyAttribute now hit an unconditional `continue` before any member-level validation. Their member types are therefore never collected or validated, so MsgPack003 (and MsgPack012 or MsgPack015 for such members) can no longer be reported for them. The new README says the analyzer still checks that members have serializable types (MsgPack003) for these types, and ledger L17 says all validation diagnostics still apply; only MsgPack011/016/017 are skipped.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a test in which a [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] class has a member annotated with a custom attribute derived from KeyAttribute. The member's type is a plain class with no [MessagePackObject] and no formatter. Expect MsgPack003 on that member. On head no MsgPack003 is reported, because the `continue` at TypeCollector.cs:921-924 (and :1083-1086 for fields) skips the member.

claim: The new ContainsKey guards on intMembers and stringMembers apply to every type, not only SuppressSourceGeneration ones. When two members share a key, the second member is now silently dropped instead of failing, and no diagnostic is raised at these call sites. If no MsgPack005-style duplicate-key diagnostic is raised elsewhere for normal types, a generated formatter would silently omit a member. That would change behaviour for types where SuppressSourceGeneration is unset, which the requirement says must not change.

receipt_plan.detail: Write a normal [MessagePackObject] class (no SuppressSourceGeneration) with two public properties both marked [Key(0)], and run VerifyCS with SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck. Assert that a duplicate-key diagnostic is reported. If the run reports no diagnostic and the generated formatter contains only one of the members, the finding is confirmed.

claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards turn a duplicate `[Key(n)]` (or a duplicate string key) into a silent first-wins. Repro: a type that is not suppressed, with `[Key(0)] int FirstValue` and `[Key(0)] int SecondValue`. On base, `Dictionary.Add` threw, so the generator or analyzer failed visibly (CS8785/AD0001). On head the second member is dropped from `intMembers`/`stringMembers`. The generated formatter never writes or reads `SecondValue`, and nothing in these hunks reports the collision. The result is silent loss of member data on round-trip. The guard is applied whether or not `SuppressSourceGeneration` is set, so it changes behaviour for unset/false, which breaks the third acceptance criterion.

It drives `CSharpGeneratorDriver` and asserts that the generator either fails, reports an error, or emits code that references `SecondValue`. Expected: passes on base (the generator throws) and fails on head (the member is silently dropped).

claim: New `continue` after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys changes which members enter the generated formatter for users who already had a mixed-key type. Before, the mismatched member was still added to intMembers/stringMembers after the diagnostic. Now it is dropped, so generated formatter output and serialized bytes change for existing code. The diagnostic is an Error, so the project normally fails to build. In the non-failing case (diagnostic suppressed or the generator run by itself) the output still differs from base.

claim: The duplicate-key guards (ContainsKey before Add) silently keep the first member and drop later ones. A user whose build was already failing may now see different diagnostics or output. This is a behaviour change in the generator for invalid input, beyond SuppressSourceGeneration.

claim: For `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`, the new early `continue` on members with a KeyAttribute-derived attribute skips everything after it in the loop body. That includes the `messagePackFormatter` lookup and the recursive collection of `item.Type`, which is what reports MsgPack003 for a member type that is not serializable. So `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] class C { [MyKey(0)] public Bar Value; }`, where `Bar` lacks `[MessagePackObject]`, no longer gets MsgPack003 on `Bar`. Ledger L17 says all validation diagnostics should still apply for suppressed types; only MsgPack011/016/017 are skipped.

receipt_plan.detail: Lines 921-924 and 1083-1086 `continue` before the `var messagePackFormatter = ...` block that follows (around lines 1050/1195). The member-type collection and MsgPack003 reporting live after that block and are therefore unreachable for derived-key members of suppressed types. Confirm with a VerifyCS test using a custom `class MyKey : KeyAttribute`, a suppressed type, and a member of a plain class type, expecting MsgPack003.
